claims.text: Intermediate-temperature heat treatment develops an optimal degree of short-range chemical order in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Short-range chemical order stabilizes a single-phase FCC structure in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Short-range chemical order lowers local free energy by modifying local bonding environments.
Short-range chemical order enhances high-temperature strength relative to processing that minimizes such order.
Short-range chemical order enhances radiation tolerance relative to processing that minimizes such order.
Short-range chemical order enhances cryogenic toughness relative to processing that minimizes such order.
Rapid quenching from high temperature minimizes short-range chemical order.
Intermediate-temperature annealing allows short-range chemical order to develop.
The degree of short-range chemical order can be measured using atom-probe tomography and diffuse scattering.
Heat treatment that permits short-range chemical order modifies lattice distortions.
The free-energy decrease caused by short-range chemical order stabilizes the single-phase FCC structure.
Enhanced phase stability improves resistance to high-temperature deformation.
Enhanced phase stability improves resistance to radiation-induced damage.
Enhanced phase stability improves the balance of ductility at cryogenic temperatures.
Annealed samples with developed short-range chemical order will exhibit sharper diffraction peaks than rapidly quenched samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit higher high-temperature yield strength than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit greater radiation-damage resistance than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit optimized cryogenic toughness relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
Rapidly quenched samples have a higher-free-energy, less phase-stable microstructure because their short-range chemical order is suppressed.
